findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued tokens to audit logs
findings.body: Whenever `recordIssuedToken` is used as intended, it passes the raw bearer token to `audit`, which writes it through `console.log`. Systems retaining console output would expose active credentials to log readers. Record only non-sensitive metadata or a one-way identifier.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` contains an absolute or protocol-relative URL, `location.assign` sends the newly authenticated user to an external destination. This creates an open-redirect phishing path. Accept only validated same-origin paths or enforce an explicit allowlist.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
Passing an attacker-controlled value such as `https://attacker.example` causes the browser to leave the trusted origin immediately after login, creating an open redirect usable for phishing. Validate against an allowlist or resolve only permitted same-origin paths.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued tokens to audit logs
findings.body:
Every real bearer token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is emitted verbatim through `console.log`, exposing an active credential to browser consoles or centralized server logs and anyone with access to them.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every call logs the raw token. In environments where console output is retained or accessible through centralized logs, anyone with lower-privileged log access can recover and replay bearer tokens until they expire.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Validate return URLs before navigating
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` originates from a login query parameter or other attacker-controlled input, an absolute or protocol-relative URL redirects authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site, enabling post-login phishing. Restrict navigation to validated same-origin paths.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
